title: Charisma Audio MC-1 Alpha — 1 kHz Reference Check
source_report_title: SME Model 12 MkII Series V Charisma Audio Mc1a

harmonic_reliability.quality_note: Steady during recording. Suitable for setup guidance.

interpretation.summary: At Entertainment Machine in Rome, the SME Model 12 MkII averaged 33.32 RPM under stylus load and measured 0.038% DIN-shaped wow and flutter. With the SME 309 and Charisma Audio MC-1 Alpha fitted, the chain measured less than 1% THD in each channel and a 5.57 dB gap between crosstalk directions.
interpretation.recommendation: The report calls for a routing and gain check followed by a repeat capture. If the crosstalk difference persists, run the General Reference Level and 1 kHz channel suite in Groove Scope Studio with matching test records.
interpretation.channel_context: Average 1 kHz separation was 22.0 dB. Right-to-left leakage was higher than left-to-right leakage throughout the captured rotations. Signal channel balance was +1.28 dB left minus right.
interpretation.rotation_context: Both speed fingerprints show a slower portion near the middle of the displayed angular scale and a faster portion towards its end, recurring over eight revolutions. The contribution of the test record and the cause of the variation were not established.

provenance.data_entry_method: Numerical results were transcribed from the original PDF report and checked against its rendered page. Reported differences preserve source precision. The venue and observations about the cartridge sample come from the measurer’s session account.
provenance.raw_audio_note: No raw test-record audio is included.
provenance.setup_metadata_source: The report title identifies the SME Model 12 MkII and Charisma Audio cartridge and labels the tonearm “Series V”. The measurer confirmed the fitted tonearm was an SME 309 and supplied the venue and session context. The manufacturer identifies the cartridge as the MC-1 Alpha. The report labels the capture input EVO4.
known_limitations: The phono stage, tracking force, physical azimuth angle, anti-skate, loading, alignment geometry, test-record identity and track, capture settings, repeat count and software versions were not recorded.
The condition of the cartridge sample was not confirmed. The cause of the crosstalk asymmetry remains open.
The results describe the playback chain as captured. The individual contributions of the cartridge, tonearm, turntable, test record and electronics were not isolated.
provenance.fingerprint_channel_assignment: Channel assignments follow the supplied filenames. Both channels show eight rotations. The angular reference between captures is unspecified.
provenance.photo_treatment: The archived source is a full-resolution JPEG from the supplied HEIC with embedded metadata stripped. The editorial photograph uses a light ImageGen retouch.
